title: Unadjusted Acclima probe swaps cause the post-2020 deep-soil drying in USCRN soil moisture, and deep soil did not stay dry after droughts (CONUS, 2009-2026)
abstract: Question: after a meteorological drought ends, does deep soil moisture stay below what station precipitation predicts? Data: NOAA USCRN daily soil moisture at 5-100 cm, station precipitation and temperature, up to 119 CONUS stations, 2009-2026; NCEI ISIS soil-probe histories (598 HydraProbe-to-Acclima swaps, 666 like-for-like replacements). Methods: leave-one-event-out precipitation-memory and threshold-bucket models, 251 common time-shift placebos, injection test; forward test fitted to 2010-2019; calendar-matched difference-in-differences at probe swaps. Results: after 554 droughts, the mean 1-12 month residual at 50-100 cm was -0.003 SD (placebo 95% range -0.067 to +0.072); the bucket model gave -0.017 SD and wet spells -0.024 SD. A deficit above about 0.13 SD (0.005 m3/m3) is unlikely. We did not reproduce a published 2013 deep deficit after the 2012 drought. After 2020, shallow layers were wetter (+0.07 to +0.48 SD) and 100 cm much drier (-0.4 to -0.8 SD) than the 2010-2019 model. The deep drying is in layers with Acclima probes, which NCEI averages without homogeneity adjustment: at 100 cm, Acclima layers were -1.39 SD and original-probe layers +0.21 SD (difference -0.037 m3/m3, 95% CI -0.070 to -0.007). At the first swap the step was -0.026 m3/m3 at 100 cm (95% CI -0.055 to -0.002) and -0.021 m3/m3 at 50 cm (-0.040 to -0.001); it grew with the number of probes swapped and with pre-swap wetness. Like-for-like replacements gave no step. The 2023-2025 network deep anomaly was -0.020 to -0.031 m3/m3 with all data but -0.009 to +0.007 m3/m3 in original-probe months. Conclusion: deep soil recovered with precipitation after droughts, and the post-2020 USCRN deep drying is mostly a sensor-transition artifact. Limitations: replaced probes were not random (failed probes in clay soils first); failure dates are unknown; simple monthly models; the cause of the post-2020 wet residual in original-probe layers is open.

display.caption: Residual of USCRN soil moisture against a precipitation-temperature model fitted to 2010-2019, by year and depth. Blue: layers with original HydraProbes. Orange: layers with at least one Acclima probe. Only the Acclima layers became much drier after 2020 at 50 and 100 cm.

Left and centre: mean residual around the first HydraProbe-to-Acclima swap of each layer (orange) and in never-changed layers over the same calendar months (grey dashed). Right: step after the swap minus control against pre-swap soil moisture at 50 and 100 cm; wetter layers dropped more.

Drought recovery test. Left: out-of-sample residual around drought end (mean and 2 SE). Centre and right: observed mean 1-12 month residual at 50-100 cm after droughts and wet spells against 251 time-shift placebos. No persistent deficit or surplus.
